remarks_1999: Double entries Whitney Archive. Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place April 1946" [notes backing inscription 1]. Whitney Archive notes backing inscriptions 1, 2 and indicates, "large semi–abstract shell. Pink mauve and yellow–red background. Note: Probably listed in 1932 cat." Pictured in 1931–32 New York (An American Place) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 50. O'Keeffe wrote, ". . . out in those hills [near Taos] I picked up mussel shells in groups all turned to stone –– probably millions of years old. They sometimes even had a little bit of the original blue color. I carried them back and left them somewhere in the unknown" (*Georgia O'Keeffe* [1976], unpaginated, text accompanying entry 76). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: The rippling center of a white shell fills the frame. The shell glows with hints of pink and orange and has a soft texture. A bright red background highlights the delicate colors of the shell.
